placements.why: src-2 states a binding system-design requirement (the pipeline must always produce a slug, via LLM id-gen or a deterministic fallback, then commit) — this is an architecture-grade commitment about system behavior, not a product/strategy/proof concern, and no strata category exists yet in this repo to hold it.
placements.title: system design commitments about pipeline behavior get tracked as their own organizational category
placements.frame: What architectural guarantee is being locked in about how the system must behave under a given input condition?

placements.title: id/slug generation always resolves via a deterministic path even when the primary method is absent or silent
placements.frame: What must be guaranteed about the pipeline's slug/id-generation and commit outcome when the primary (LLM id-gen) path is unavailable — and does the deterministic slugify fallback actually cover every gap the primary path leaves?
placements.why: src-1 names the precondition (a memory arrived with no explicit id) and src-2 names the pipeline's required response (produce a slug via LLM id-gen or the deterministic slugify fallback, then commit) — together they name a recurring design subject future envelopes about this pipeline will keep feeding (does the fallback path hold, does the commit always succeed), not a one-time fact about this single submission. src-1 is evidence for the same leaf rather than its own leaf, per the narrative grain test.
